blocks.text: 《华尔街日报》看到了Anthropic的IPO文件草案：6个月营收163亿美元，账面亏损807亿美元，并承诺约4500亿美元用于算力

inlines.text: 《华尔街日报》看到了Anthropic的IPO文件草案：6个月营收163亿美元，账面亏损807亿美元，并承诺约4500亿美元用于算力

blocks.text: Anthropic上半年在算力和基础设施上花费近90亿美元，超过其2025年全年的73亿美元，而其新的招股说明书草案显示，这笔账单正攀升至7500亿美元。
三大云厂商占据了未来7到10年2520亿美元的固定付款：1110亿美元给Google，1100亿美元给Amazon Web Services，310亿美元给Microsoft，无论Anthropic是否使用这些容量，都需支付。
芯片构成下一层。Anthropic通过Broadcom拥有超过1600亿美元的Google芯片租赁，以及从Nscale和Lambda租用Nvidia GPU的最高860亿美元，这些合同分别于2033年和2034年到期。
另有1500亿美元的交易仍在谈判中。

inlines.text: 另有1500亿美元的交易仍在谈判中。

blocks.text: 资金并非唯一限制。Anthropic表示，Amazon、Google和Microsoft不愿提供其想要的全部容量，且它们现在将其视为竞争对手。它还依赖较新的数据中心运营商，并警告这些运营商历史较短，站点可靠性可能较低。
有一笔交易未具名：9月草案中最高845亿美元的xAI容量协议，该协议持续至2029年，且大部分可提前90天通知取消。它可能包含在约1120亿美元、基本不可取消的4500亿美元云总算力中未逐项列出的部分， alongside 预计超过200亿美元的AMD容量，也可能已被放弃。
在风险因素中，Anthropic表示，其模型造成的某些损害（如数据盗窃或安全漏洞）需由其承担责任，且灾难性AI事件可能超出其所能购买的任何保险。
收入也很集中：2个未具名客户贡献了上半年约20%的销售额，Anthropic预计在可预见的未来，一小群客户将继续提供很大一部分收入。
它还将日益有组织地反对数据中心列为业务风险，并表示其高知名度可能给其项目带来额外审查。
WSJ saw Anthropic’s draft IPO papers: $16.3B revenue in 6 months, $80.7B loss on paper, and about $450B promised for compute

inlines.text: WSJ saw Anthropic’s draft IPO papers: $16.3B revenue in 6 months, $80.7B loss on paper, and about $450B promised for compute

blocks.text: Anthropic spent nearly $9B on compute and infrastructure in the first half, more than its $7.3B total for 2025, and its new draft prospectus shows the bill climbing toward $750B.

The 3 big clouds account for $252B of fixed payments over the next 7 to 10 years: $111B to Google, $110B to Amazon Web Services and $31B to Microsoft, all due whether or not Anthropic uses the capacity.

Chips form the next layer. Anthropic has more than $160B in Google chip leases through Broadcom and up to $86B for Nvidia GPUs rented from Nscale and Lambda, with those contracts ending in 2033 and 2034.
Another $150B in deals is still under negotiation.

inlines.text: Another $150B in deals is still under negotiation.

blocks.text: Money isn’t the only limit. Anthropic says Amazon, Google and Microsoft wouldn’t supply all the capacity it wanted, and they now treat it as a rival. It is also leaning on newer data center operators, which it warns have short histories and possibly less reliable sites.

One deal goes unnamed: the September draft’s up-to-$84.5B xAI capacity agreement, which runs through 2029 and can largely be cancelled on 90 days’ notice. It may sit inside the roughly $112B of the mostly noncancelable $450B cloud total that isn’t itemized, alongside AMD capacity expected to top $20B, or it may have been dropped.

In its risk factors, Anthropic says it is liable for some damage its models cause, such as data theft or security breaches, and that a catastrophic AI incident could exceed any insurance it could buy.
Revenue is concentrated too: 2 unnamed customers delivered about 20% of first-half sales, and Anthropic expects a small group of customers to keep supplying a large share for the foreseeable future.
It also lists increasingly organized opposition to data centers as a business risk and says its high profile could bring extra scrutiny to its projects.
